title: Hardware health
description: Is the physical hardware about to fail? Disk SMART, CPU and board temperatures, fans, AC power and the GPU, per node. Open it after a Disk*, Host*Hot, HostOnBattery or Gpu* alert, or on the weekly review to see what is degrading.

panels.title: Is the hardware about to fail?
On battery
panels.description: Laptop nodes (pve2, pve3) whose AC adapter is not supplying power (rule HostOnBattery, 1 minute, critical). pve1 is a desktop and has no such sensor. Read it knowing that the batteries do not hold a node up (docs/hardware.md): a house power cut takes the node down instead of showing here, so this goes red for an unplugged adapter, and a real cut shows as the node unreachable and can leave a step in the unsafe-shutdown counter below.

panels.title: SMART failing
panels.description: Disks whose SMART overall health says FAILED (rule DiskSmartFailing, critical, no delay). Red means copy the data off now (docs/runbooks/disk-rescue.md). Whole fleet, not filtered by the Node selector.

panels.title: Disks with unreadable sectors
panels.description: Disks with pending or offline-uncorrectable sectors (rule DiskPendingSectors, critical). Any number above 0 is data the disk can no longer read: pve3's old HDD died this way with 8,448. Copy the data off and plan the replacement. Only the SATA disks report these counters.

panels.title: Reallocated sectors grew, 24 h
panels.description: Disks whose reallocated-sector count rose in the last day (rule DiskReallocatedSectorsGrowing, warning). A steady count is a disk that remapped some sectors once and held (pve2's HDD has had 9 since 2026-10-09); growth is a disk that is degrading. The table below shows the 7-day change per disk.

panels.title: Hottest disk
panels.description: The hottest SATA disk by its own SMART temperature (rule DiskHot: above 55 C for 30 minutes, warning). pve1's NVMe is not in it: the collector reads no NVMe temperature, see the disk temperature panel for the hwmon reading.

panels.title: Hottest CPU
panels.description: The hottest CPU package across the three nodes (rule HostCpuHot: above 90 C for 10 minutes, warning), picked by hwmon chip name: Intel coretemp on pve2 and pve3, AMD k10temp on pve1. The Ryzen throttles near 95 C.

targets.expr: max(node_hwmon_temp_celsius{job="node", instance=~"pve.*"} * on (instance, chip) group_left () (node_hwmon_chip_names{job="node", chip_name=~"coretemp|k10temp"} * 0 + 1))

panels.title: GPU temperature
panels.description: Temperature of the RTX 3060 in the `ai` VM (rule GpuHot: 83 C or more for 5 minutes, warning; the card slows itself down from about 83 C). The VM is on demand and off most of the time, so 'ai off' is the normal reading and not a fault. The GPU row below keeps the last 30 days.

panels.title: GPU hardware slowdown
panels.description: 1 when the board itself pulls the GPU clocks down, for heat (hw_thermal_slowdown) or because the PSU asserts the power brake (hw_power_brake_slowdown) (rule GpuHardwareSlowdown, 5 minutes). The ordinary 170 W power cap does not count. 'ai off' is the normal reading while the VM is off.

panels.title: Disks
panels.description: Every disk the SMART collector sees (it runs every 15 minutes, never a self-test). Health FAILED, Pending or Uncorrectable above 0 (rules DiskSmartFailing, DiskPendingSectors) are red; Reallocated, 7 d above 0 is orange (rule DiskReallocatedSectorsGrowing); Temp turns orange at 55 C (rule DiskHot). Wear value is SMART attribute 177 as the drive normalises it (100 when new, the drive's own threshold is lower), reported by pve3's SSD only. A blank cell means the drive does not report that attribute; pve1's NVMe reports health and nothing else, so it has no temperature, hours or wear here.

targets.expr: max by (instance, disk, device_model) ((smartmon_device_smart_healthy{instance=~"$instance"}) * on (instance, disk) group_left (device_model) (smartmon_device_info{type!="nvme"} or label_replace(label_replace(node_nvme_info{job="node"}, "disk", "/dev/$1", "device", "(.*)"), "device_model", "$1", "model", "(.*)")))

max by (instance, disk, device_model) ((smartmon_temperature_celsius_raw_value{instance=~"$instance"}) * on (instance, disk) group_left (device_model) (smartmon_device_info{type!="nvme"} or label_replace(label_replace(node_nvme_info{job="node"}, "disk", "/dev/$1", "device", "(.*)"), "device_model", "$1", "model", "(.*)")))

max by (instance, disk, device_model) ((smartmon_power_on_hours_raw_value{instance=~"$instance"}) * on (instance, disk) group_left (device_model) (smartmon_device_info{type!="nvme"} or label_replace(label_replace(node_nvme_info{job="node"}, "disk", "/dev/$1", "device", "(.*)"), "device_model", "$1", "model", "(.*)")))

max by (instance, disk, device_model) ((smartmon_reallocated_sector_ct_raw_value{instance=~"$instance"}) * on (instance, disk) group_left (device_model) (smartmon_device_info{type!="nvme"} or label_replace(label_replace(node_nvme_info{job="node"}, "disk", "/dev/$1", "device", "(.*)"), "device_model", "$1", "model", "(.*)")))

max by (instance, disk, device_model) ((smartmon_reallocated_sector_ct_raw_value{instance=~"$instance"} - (smartmon_reallocated_sector_ct_raw_value{instance=~"$instance"} offset 7d)) * on (instance, disk) group_left (device_model) (smartmon_device_info{type!="nvme"} or label_replace(label_replace(node_nvme_info{job="node"}, "disk", "/dev/$1", "device", "(.*)"), "device_model", "$1", "model", "(.*)")))

max by (instance, disk, device_model) ((smartmon_current_pending_sector_raw_value{instance=~"$instance"}) * on (instance, disk) group_left (device_model) (smartmon_device_info{type!="nvme"} or label_replace(label_replace(node_nvme_info{job="node"}, "disk", "/dev/$1", "device", "(.*)"), "device_model", "$1", "model", "(.*)")))

max by (instance, disk, device_model) ((smartmon_offline_uncorrectable_raw_value{instance=~"$instance"}) * on (instance, disk) group_left (device_model) (smartmon_device_info{type!="nvme"} or label_replace(label_replace(node_nvme_info{job="node"}, "disk", "/dev/$1", "device", "(.*)"), "device_model", "$1", "model", "(.*)")))

max by (instance, disk, device_model) ((smartmon_wear_leveling_count_value{instance=~"$instance"}) * on (instance, disk) group_left (device_model) (smartmon_device_info{type!="nvme"} or label_replace(label_replace(node_nvme_info{job="node"}, "disk", "/dev/$1", "device", "(.*)"), "device_model", "$1", "model", "(.*)")))

panels.title: Disk temperature
panels.description: SMART temperature per SATA disk, plus pve1's NVMe from its hwmon sensor (the SMART collector has no NVMe temperature, and rule DiskHot does not cover the NVMe). The dashed line is 55 C (rule DiskHot, 30 minutes). Look for a disk that runs hotter than its neighbours or climbs over weeks: dust or a failing fan.

targets.expr: max by (instance) (node_hwmon_temp_celsius{job="node", instance=~"pve.*", instance=~"$instance", sensor="temp1"} * on (instance, chip) group_left () (node_hwmon_chip_names{job="node", instance=~"pve.*", chip_name="nvme"} * 0 + 1))

panels.title: Bad sectors
panels.description: Sector counters per disk over the range. Pending or uncorrectable above 0 is critical (rule DiskPendingSectors). A reallocated line that steps up is rule DiskReallocatedSectorsGrowing; a flat line, even above 0, is a disk that stabilised. Only the SATA disks report these.

panels.title: SMART data age
panels.description: Seconds since each node's SMART file was written. The collector runs every 15 minutes; over 1 hour (orange, rule HostTextfileCollectorStale) every disk alert above is blind. After a power cut the laptops boot with a wrong clock and this reads months until the next run clears it.

panels.title: CPU package temperature
panels.description: CPU temperature per node, by hwmon chip name as rule HostCpuHot does it. The dashed line is 90 C (10 minutes, warning). A baseline that creeps up over weeks at the same load means dried paste or a clogged fan, long before the alert.

targets.expr: max by (instance) (node_hwmon_temp_celsius{job="node", instance=~"pve.*", instance=~"$instance"} * on (instance, chip) group_left () (node_hwmon_chip_names{job="node", instance=~"pve.*", chip_name=~"coretemp|k10temp"} * 0 + 1))

panels.title: Board and drive sensors
panels.description: The other temperature sensors per node: the ACPI zone, the chipset (pch_skylake) on the laptops and the NVMe on pve1. No alert watches these; they explain a hot CPU (a chipset hot as well means a case problem, not a busy CPU).

targets.expr: max by (instance, chip_name) (node_hwmon_temp_celsius{job="node", instance=~"pve.*", instance=~"$instance"} * on (instance, chip) group_left (chip_name) (node_hwmon_chip_names{job="node", instance=~"pve.*", chip_name!~"coretemp|k10temp"} * 0 + 1))

panels.title: Fan speed
panels.description: The CPU fan of the two laptop nodes. No alert watches it. A fan at 0 rpm while the CPU is warm is a dead fan; a speed that rises for the same load is a clogging heatsink. pve1 exposes no fan sensor, so it has no line here.

panels.title: CPU thermal throttle events
panels.description: Times per second the CPU slowed itself down for heat (kernel thermal-throttle counters: pve2 and pve3 report them, pve1's Ryzen exposes none). No alert watches it. The line should be flat at 0; any rise means the temperature panel is hiding a CPU that is being held back.

panels.title: AC power
panels.description: Whether the laptop nodes' AC adapter is supplying power (rule HostOnBattery). Red is BATTERY. pve1 is a desktop with no power-supply sensor. Because the batteries do not keep a node up (docs/hardware.md), a house power cut does not draw a red bar: the node just disappears. Read the unsafe-shutdown panel for those.

panels.title: Battery
panels.description: The kernel's view of each laptop battery. 'Not charging' while on AC is normal; 'Discharging' means AC is lost. There is no charge or capacity reading: BAT0 reports none (docs/hardware.md), so remaining runtime cannot be shown here.

panels.title: Unsafe shutdowns
panels.description: The SSD's own count of power losses without a clean shutdown (SMART attribute 192). Each step up is a hard power-off: a house power cut, a held power button or a crash reset. It is the only after-the-fact power-cut record the lab has while the batteries carry nothing. No alert watches it. Only pve2's Kingston SSD reports it.

panels.title: GPU temperature over time
panels.description: RTX 3060 temperature. The dashed line is 83 C (rule GpuHot, 5 minutes, warning). The VM is on demand, so this is empty while it is off (by design, not a fault) and shows the last 30 days whatever the dashboard's range is. A run that sits at the line means dust, a dead fan or a hot room.

panels.title: GPU fan
panels.description: GPU fan speed as a share of its maximum. No alert watches it. Empty while the VM is off; last 30 days. A fan at 0 % under load with a rising temperature is a stopped fan.

panels.title: GPU power draw vs limit
panels.description: Power the GPU draws against its power limit (170 W). Sitting on the limit under load is normal and is not alerted (sw_power_cap); a draw that cannot reach the limit with the clocks pulled down is the power brake of rule GpuHardwareSlowdown. Empty while the VM is off; last 30 days.

panels.title: GPU graphics clock
panels.description: Graphics clock against the card's maximum. A clock far under the maximum while the GPU is busy and the power draw is below its limit means the board is holding it down (see the slowdown reasons). Idle clocks are low by design. Empty while the VM is off; last 30 days.

panels.title: GPU memory used
panels.description: VRAM in use against the card's 12 GiB. No alert: vLLM and SGLang pre-allocate about 90 % of VRAM by design (rules/gpu.yml), so a high line is normal. Empty while the VM is off; last 30 days.

panels.title: GPU slowdown reasons
panels.description: The three hardware clock-event reasons that rule GpuHardwareSlowdown watches. Any red bar longer than 5 minutes alerts: thermal means airflow, power brake means the PSU or its PCIe cable cannot keep up. The normal software power cap is not shown. Empty while the VM is off; last 30 days.
